review_principle: Outer envelope of accepted literature scenarios and uncertainties; no common confidence level.

21.name: Vela (PSR B0833−45)
21.marker_policy: Marker retained from WEB at 21.4 kyr (geometric midpoint of P20 17–27 kyr) and 4.24e32 erg/s (P20 R = 13 km fit); a reference location, not a best estimate.
21.notes: Rounded selected bounds, not exhaustive confidence limits. The 40 kyr ceiling is conditional on extrapolating the low braking index and torque law over the lifetime. The retained luminosity marker lies close to the upper edge; see audit section 3.

33.name: PSR B2334+61
33.notes: Age span is a display placeholder, not an adopted physical interval at 3.1 kpc. P20 13 km fit is distance compatible, not refit to the accepted distance. Direct McGowan alternatives excluded; inherited provenance retained. Retained orange box is a working cold-source comparison, not an envelope of the near-distance branch: Chen et al. 2025 find ~0.95 kpc; fixed-flux rescaling gives lower luminosities outside the box, not a self-consistent refit. Suzuki kinematic age lower limit is conditional; Dincel 22.7 kyr calculation requires clarification.

20.name: PSR B0656+14 / Monogem
20.marker_policy: Retain previous WEB luminosity and fallback age for comparison; no new best estimate selected.
20.notes: Selected envelope deliberately retains the unreconciled P20 high luminosity; no common confidence level. See primary-source checks in audit section 4.

14.name: PSR J0205+6449 / 3C 58
14.notes: Age 0.8–7 kyr retained (decision 2026-11-20): young decelerating models (Kothes 2013) and several-kyr optical/radio scenarios; 0.8 is a rounded continuity choice, not the minimum of Kothes, and 7 kyr is a PWN expansion timescale, not a rigorous upper bound (for steady PWN growth R ∝ t^1.2 inside freely expanding ejecta, t ≈ 1.2 × 7 ≈ 8.4 kyr). SN 1181 is not assumed; Pa 30 is its likely remnant. Luminosity (0.8–3.4) × 10³² erg/s: the small-area lower edge 2 × 10³¹ is removed; single interval, no split by spectral interpretation. The conditional hidden-surface limit < 10²⁸ erg/s (kT ≈ 4 eV) is not plotted. Open: check whether the Kothes 0.63–1.6 kyr range is derived independently of the 1181 date. No common confidence level or equal endpoint weights.
14.marker_policy: Marker retained at the WEB location, 819.5 yr (about 819 yr) and 1.9e32 erg/s; a display location, not a best estimate or an adoption of the SN 1181 association.

13.name: Cas A / CXOU J232327.8+584842
13.notes: Fesen et al. explosion epoch 1681 ± 19 CE converted to 307–345 yr at the fixed reference epoch 2007; uncertainty is conditional on the ejecta model. The previous 320–339 yr WEB interval is retained only in imported measurements and does not represent this uncertainty. The catalogue marker 326.2 yr is retained as a display location; luminosity range is unchanged.

3.name: Vela Jr / CXOU J085201.4−461753

age_scenarios.assumption: Sedov-Taylor using two NW-rim expansion measurements

3.notes: Adopt age 1.6–5.1 kyr and Ho2026 cool-surface luminosity 1.3–4.0 × 10^32 erg/s as error bars only. Ho range spans model medians, not a common statistical confidence interval; geometric age marker is the midpoint of 1.6–5.1 kyr and is illustrative. Marino2024 results are compatible in order of magnitude but refer to different spectral components and partially shared data. P20 high carbon branch excluded from adopted range. Distance, spectral model and wind-age caveats remain. Distance 1.41 (1.27–1.55) kpc (Suherli2026) adopted 2026-11-20, consistent with the Ho2026 analysis; distance-only rescaling of P20 or M24 values remains invalid.

48.name: PSR B1727−47
48.notes: Age interval adopted 18 November 2026 as a review range, without a common confidence level. Original luminosity ceiling and marker retained; spectral provenance/component caveats remain in the audit.

46.name: PSR J0007+7303
46.notes: Age 9–13 kyr. Nominal ceiling L∞ < 3e31 erg/s, documented as the NSA local-temperature conversion of the Caraveo et al. (2010) 3-sigma limit; conservative ceiling about 1e32 erg/s (BB, 10 km as physical radius), drawn as a dotted extension. Pulsed hot-spot component excluded from the cooling comparison. Open action: look for a newer reanalysis of the archival Chandra/XMM data, or refit independently (modern atmosphere, R about 12 km, pulsar/PWN separation).

ceiling_conventions.reference: Caraveo2010, 3-sigma whole-surface limits for a 10 km star at 1.4 kpc: T < 5.3e5 K (BB), T < 4.8e5 K (NSA)
ceiling_conventions.note: Conversions keep R = 10 km and do not refit; R = 12–13 km raises each ceiling by up to about 1.5–1.7 times, partly offset by a lower temperature limit; 1.7 kpc adds about 20%.

17.name: CXOU J061705.3+222127 / IC 443
17.notes: Adopt age 3–20 kyr, distance 1.6–1.7 kpc and L∞=(1.0–3.5)e32 erg/s. Rounded scenario envelope from BB/NSA interpretations, their quoted errors and conditional distance scaling; no common confidence level or spectral refit. Exclude old Chevalier and NS cooling-model ages from age selection. BB small-area versus NSA whole-surface interpretation remains a caveat.
17.marker_policy: Geometric age midpoint for display; previous catalogue luminosity 2.6e32 retained as reference, not a new best fit.

30.name: PSR B1951+32 / CTB 80
30.marker_policy: Retain 64 kyr age display anchor; replace detected hot-spot luminosity by whole-surface ceiling.
30.notes: Accepted 18 November 2026: age 45–85 kyr, distance 1–2 kpc, whole-surface L_inf < 3.8e32 erg/s. Published 3-sigma fixed-12-km BB ceiling retained at reference distance 2 kpc; no distance refit or invented luminosity lower bound. Hot-spot measurement remains in historical records, excluded from current cooling point.
30.temperature_upper_limit_reference: Li2005 whole-surface fixed-12-km BB, 3 sigma at 2 kpc

16.name: PSR J0538+2817 / S147
16.marker_policy: Display marker at geometric midpoint of luminosity envelope (~8.25e32 erg/s) and 30 kyr kinematic midpoint; both are fiducial locations within the adopted envelope, not best estimates.
16.notes: Luminosity decision 2026-11-20. Outer envelope: low end V13 BB+PL at 1.3 kpc gives 5.0e32 erg/s; high end P20 NSA family at 1.47 kpc gives 1.36e33 erg/s. Both distances are within Kochanek et al. (2024) 90% interval of 1.30–1.47 kpc. No rescaling applied; each fit retained at its own cited distance (Option A). The web distance update to 1.37 kpc median does not invalidate either endpoint. Primary spectral paper: McGowan et al. (2003), XMM-Newton. No post-P20 reanalysis at the Kochanek distance is available. BB+PL and NSA models give genuinely different luminosity estimates; both are included in the outer envelope as the review principle requires.
